title: Early Investment Snowballs for Low-Skill Children: Average Marginal Returns and the Dynamics of Skill Formation
abstract: arXiv:2610.12509v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Program evaluations routinely find larger returns to investment in low-skill children, while structural models of skill formation typically find that skill and investment are complements. I show that these findings are not in tension: they measure different objects. The Beckerian schedule of returns (BSR) is the elasticity of output with respect to an input, holding all inputs at fixed values; average marginal returns (AMR) average that elasticity over the joint distribution of inputs. Revisiting Cunha, Heckman, and Schennach (2010)'s model of child skill formation on the Children of the NLSY79, I find that skill and investment are complements, but that low-skill children receive so much less investment that their AMR to investment is higher in early childhood --- a pattern that reverses at later ages. The framework also provides a natural way to sign bias from curvature in log-linear models with interaction terms, which conflate the BSR

translated_title: 低技能儿童的早期投资滚雪球效应：平均边际回报与技能形成的动态过程
translated_abstract: 项目评估通常发现对低技能儿童的投资回报更大，而技能形成的结构模型一般发现技能与投资是互补的。我证明这些发现并不矛盾：它们衡量的是不同的对象。贝克尔回报曲线（BSR）是在所有投入保持固定值时，产出对某一投入的弹性；平均边际回报（AMR）则是该弹性在投入联合分布上的平均值。通过重新审视 Cunha、Heckman 和 Schennach（2010）在 NLSY79 儿童样本上的儿童技能形成模型，我发现技能与投资确实是互补的，但低技能儿童获得的投资如此之少，以至于他们在儿童早期的投资平均边际回报更高——这一模式在较晚年龄段发生逆转。该框架还提供了一种自然的方法来确定含交互项的对数线性模型中由曲率引起的偏差符号，这类模型混淆了 BSR
tldr: 论文通过区分贝克尔回报曲线（BSR）与平均边际回报（AMR）这两个不同概念，化解了项目评估与结构模型关于低技能儿童投资回报的表面矛盾，并发现低技能儿童在幼年因投资匮乏而拥有更高的平均边际投资回报，这一优势在较晚年龄段发生逆转。
en_tdlr: By distinguishing the Beckerian schedule of returns (BSR) from average marginal returns (AMR), the paper resolves the apparent tension between program evaluations and structural models, showing that low-skill children exhibit higher average marginal returns to investment in early childhood due to their low investment levels—a pattern that reverses at later ages.
